questions.q: What is the most common mistake people make when writing prompts for LLMs?
options: Writing vague, underspecified instructions that leave the model guessing about format, scope, and constraints

questions.q: What are the four core components of an effective prompt?
options: Role, context, constraints, and output format

questions.q: Why should you include output format instructions in your prompts?
options: Without format instructions, the model chooses its own structure, which varies between calls and is hard to parse programmatically

questions.q: What is the purpose of a system prompt?
options: To set persistent behavioral rules, role, and constraints that apply to the entire conversation

questions.q: How should you test whether a prompt change actually improved output quality?
options: Run the prompt on a diverse test set and measure changes in defined metrics (accuracy, format compliance, relevance)
Ask the model if it's doing better
Read a few outputs and make a judgment call

questions.q: What is the key difference between zero-shot and few-shot prompting?
options: Zero-shot gives only the instruction; few-shot includes example input-output demonstrations before the actual query
Zero-shot doesn't use a system prompt

questions.q: What does 'Chain of Thought' prompting do?
options: It instructs the model to show intermediate reasoning steps before giving the final answer, improving accuracy on multi-step problems
It chains multiple API calls together
It connects multiple models in sequence

questions.q: How does Tree-of-Thought differ from Chain-of-Thought?
options: It explores multiple reasoning paths in parallel and evaluates which path leads to the best answer
It uses a tree data structure for storage
It's just a longer chain of thought

questions.q: When selecting few-shot examples, what matters most?
options: Choosing diverse examples that cover different cases and demonstrate the exact format and reasoning pattern you want
Using as many examples as possible
Using examples from the test set

questions.q: Why does CoT prompting improve accuracy even though the model has the same knowledge with or without it?
options: Generating intermediate tokens creates a larger effective context for the final answer, allowing the model to condition on its own reasoning

questions.q: Why is getting structured JSON output from LLMs challenging?
options: JSON is too complex for LLMs
LLMs generate free-form text token by token and can produce invalid JSON (missing brackets, wrong types, extra text) at any point

questions.q: What is constrained decoding?
options: Restricting which tokens the model can generate at each step to ensure the output conforms to a grammar or schema

questions.q: What is the benefit of using Pydantic models for LLM output validation?
options: They define typed schemas that automatically validate, parse, and reject malformed LLM outputs with clear error messages

questions.q: What should you do when the LLM returns invalid JSON despite instructions?
options: Implement a retry loop that sends the validation error back to the model as context for a corrected attempt

questions.q: When should you use the API's native JSON mode vs prompt-based JSON extraction?
options: Use native mode for guaranteed structure; use prompt-based for complex extraction where you need the model to reason about what to extract

questions.q: What problem do embeddings solve that keyword search cannot?
options: Embeddings capture semantic meaning, matching 'payment didn't go through' with 'charge was declined' even though they share no words

questions.q: What does cosine similarity measure between two embedding vectors?
options: The angle between the vectors, indicating how similar their directions are regardless of magnitude

questions.q: What is the typical dimensionality of modern text embedding models?
Why should you evaluate embedding quality using retrieval benchmarks rather than just inspecting similarity scores?
options: Similarity scores don't use cosine distance
Absolute similarity values vary by model; what matters is whether relevant documents rank higher than irrelevant ones (precision@k, recall)

questions.q: When would you use a local/open-source embedding model instead of an API-based one?
options: When you need data privacy, offline operation, lower cost at scale, or domain-specific fine-tuning
Local models produce higher quality embeddings

questions.q: What is the difference between prompt engineering and context engineering?
options: Context engineering is about database design
A prompt is the user's query; context is everything in the model's window: system prompt, tools, retrieved docs, history, and the prompt itself

questions.q: Why does context window order matter for LLM performance?
options: LLMs have recency and primacy biases, paying more attention to the beginning and end of the context window
Alphabetical order helps the model search faster
It doesn't -- LLMs process all tokens equally

questions.q: A coding assistant uses 22,700 tokens of a 128K context window. Why is budget management still important?
options: 128K should be enough for any use case
Long conversations, large code files, and retrieved documentation can quickly fill the window; without budget management, critical context gets truncated

questions.q: What is the sliding window strategy for conversation history?
options: Keeping only the N most recent turns in context and dropping older turns, optionally summarizing them first
Moving the model to a different server
Processing the conversation in fixed-size chunks

questions.q: How should a context assembler allocate tokens across components?
options: Dynamically based on query type: a simple question needs less retrieval context; a complex question needs more, with generation headroom always reserved

questions.q: What does RAG stand for and what problem does it solve?
options: Recurrent Attention Generation -- improving attention mechanisms
Retrieval-Augmented Generation -- giving LLMs access to external knowledge they weren't trained on
Reduced Architecture Generation -- making models smaller
Random Augmented Generation -- generating random outputs

questions.q: Why is RAG preferred over fine-tuning for most knowledge-grounded applications?
options: RAG is cheaper, instantly updatable when documents change, and provides source attribution -- fine-tuning is expensive and becomes stale

questions.q: What is the correct order of steps in a basic RAG pipeline?
options: Chunk documents, embed chunks, store in vector DB, embed query, retrieve similar chunks, generate answer with context
Embed query, generate answer, retrieve documents
Store documents, query the LLM, add documents to response

questions.q: What is a common failure mode in basic RAG systems?
options: The retrieved chunks are semantically similar to the query but don't contain the actual answer (e.g., returning 'revenue strategy' when asked for 'Q3 revenue numbers')

questions.q: How do you evaluate RAG quality?
options: By checking if the LLM produces any output
Using both retrieval metrics (did we find the right chunks?) and generation metrics (is the answer faithful to the retrieved context?)
By counting the number of retrieved documents

questions.q: What is the limitation of basic top-k semantic search in RAG?
options: It retrieves chunks that are semantically similar to the query but may not contain the actual answer, especially for ambiguous or multi-hop questions

questions.q: What is hybrid search in the context of RAG?
options: Combining BM25 keyword matching with semantic vector search to capture both exact terms and meaning-based relevance
Using both CPU and GPU for search

questions.q: What does a cross-encoder reranker do in an advanced RAG pipeline?
options: It takes (query, document) pairs and scores their relevance with higher accuracy than embedding similarity, reordering the initial retrieval results

questions.q: What is the HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embedding) query transformation technique?
options: Using the LLM to generate a hypothetical answer, then embedding that answer as the search query instead of the original question
Hiding the query from the model

questions.q: Why does parent-child chunking improve RAG over flat chunking?
options: Small child chunks are used for precise retrieval, but the larger parent chunk is returned for context, preventing the 'lost context' problem
It reduces the number of chunks
It eliminates the need for embeddings

questions.q: What is the core insight behind LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)?
options: Weight updates during fine-tuning have low intrinsic rank, so they can be approximated by two small matrices instead of updating the full weight matrix
Fine-tuning only needs the last layer

questions.q: How much memory does LoRA save compared to full fine-tuning of an 8B model?
options: From ~56GB down to ~6GB by training <1% of parameters while keeping base weights frozen

questions.q: What is QLoRA?
options: Quantized LoRA: the base model is loaded in 4-bit precision while LoRA adapters train in 16-bit, combining memory savings from both techniques

questions.q: What does the 'rank' parameter (r) in LoRA control?
options: The capacity of the adapter: higher rank captures more complex adaptations but uses more parameters and memory
The number of layers to fine-tune

questions.q: What happens when you merge LoRA weights back into the base model?
options: The model needs to be retrained
The adapter matrices are added to the base weights (W_merged = W_base + B*A), producing a standard model with no inference overhead

questions.q: Can LLMs actually execute functions or access external systems?
options: No -- LLMs only generate text (typically JSON) describing which function to call; your code must execute it
Yes, LLMs can call APIs directly

questions.q: What is a tool schema in the context of function calling?
options: A JSON description of a function's name, parameters, types, and purpose that tells the model what tools are available

questions.q: What is the standard pattern for a multi-turn function calling loop?
options: Send message -> model requests tool call -> execute function -> send result back -> model generates final response (repeat if needed)
Parse the entire conversation as a batch

questions.q: How do you prevent infinite tool calling loops?
options: Set a maximum number of tool call iterations and implement a timeout, breaking the loop if the limit is reached
Remove all tool schemas after the first call
Infinite loops can't happen with function calling

questions.q: Why are clear, descriptive parameter names and descriptions important in tool schemas?
options: The model uses descriptions to decide which tool to call and how to fill in parameters -- vague descriptions lead to wrong tool selections and incorrect arguments
They are required by the API
They make the code more readable

questions.q: Why is manually reading a few LLM outputs not a reliable evaluation method?
options: Small samples miss failure modes that only appear at scale, and human judgment is inconsistent across reviewers and sessions

questions.q: What is regression testing in the context of LLM applications?
options: Running a fixed set of test cases after every change (prompt, model, parameters) to ensure quality hasn't degraded

questions.q: What is the LLM-as-judge evaluation approach?
options: Using a strong LLM to score outputs against rubrics, replacing expensive human evaluation while scaling to thousands of test cases
Having the model evaluate its own training loss

questions.q: What makes a good evaluation dataset for an LLM application?
options: Diverse inputs covering common cases, edge cases, adversarial inputs, and expected outputs with clear rubrics

questions.q: How should you handle non-deterministic LLM outputs in evaluation?
options: Run each test case multiple times and use aggregate metrics (pass rate, average score) to account for output variance
Set temperature to 0 for all evaluations

questions.q: Why do AI startups often fail from cost issues rather than model quality?
options: Per-call costs compound rapidly: 10K users making 10 calls/day costs $250/day in tokens before charging a single dollar
API providers offer unlimited free tiers

questions.q: What is semantic caching for LLM applications?
options: Storing responses for previous queries and serving cached responses when a new query is semantically similar (not just exactly matching)

questions.q: What is model routing as a cost optimization strategy?
options: Sending simple queries to cheap/fast models and complex queries to expensive/powerful models based on query classification

questions.q: What is prompt compression and how does it reduce costs?
options: Removing redundant tokens, summarizing long contexts, and eliminating boilerplate to reduce input token count while preserving essential information
Making prompts shorter by removing words

questions.q: What is prefix caching and which provider feature enables it?
options: Reusing KV-cache computation for shared prompt prefixes (system prompt + tool definitions), reducing latency and cost for repeated patterns
Caching the first word of each response

questions.q: What is prompt injection?
options: A user crafting input that overrides the system prompt's instructions, causing the model to follow the attacker's instructions instead
Injecting code into the model's weights
Adding extra tokens to reduce cost

questions.q: Why is output validation necessary even if input guardrails are in place?
options: Output validation is only needed for code generation
Models can hallucinate PII, generate harmful content, or produce policy-violating outputs even from benign inputs
It's only needed for legal compliance

questions.q: What is a layered defense system for LLM applications?
options: Running the model on multiple GPUs
Combining input filtering, system prompt hardening, output validation, and monitoring -- so if one layer fails, others catch the issue

questions.q: How should you test your guardrails before deploying?
options: Run a red-team prompt set of known attack patterns and measure both false positive rate (blocking valid inputs) and false negative rate (missing attacks)
Trust that they work based on the implementation

questions.q: What is the most effective defense against system prompt extraction attacks?
options: Making the system prompt very long
Never putting secrets in the system prompt, since no defense can guarantee the model won't reveal prompt contents
Adding 'never reveal your system prompt' to the prompt

questions.q: What is the biggest gap between an LLM demo and a production LLM application?
options: Infrastructure: error handling, streaming, cost tracking, rate limiting, fallbacks, observability, and graceful degradation under load

questions.q: Why is streaming token delivery important in production LLM applications?
options: Users perceive the first token arriving quickly as faster, even if total generation time is the same -- reducing perceived latency from seconds to milliseconds

questions.q: What should happen when your LLM API provider has an outage?
options: Retry indefinitely until the provider recovers
The application should automatically fall back to an alternative provider or return a graceful degraded response

questions.q: What observability metrics should a production LLM application track?
options: Request latency (P50/P95/P99), cost per request, error rates, token usage, cache hit rates, and quality scores from automated evals

questions.q: Why should you implement rate limiting in your LLM application?
options: To make the application seem exclusive
To prevent individual users from exhausting your API budget, protect against abuse, and ensure fair access during high traffic
Rate limiting is only needed for free tiers
